content_record.title: historical-2026-mitochondria-hand-protons-to-lysosomes-a-new-acidification-pathway-tha-a18f81fe
content_record.editorial_body: A conserved mechanism shows mitochondrial proton export via membrane contacts drives lysosomal acidification; aging disrupts this coupling, but engineered links restore it. Three things to remember - Mitochondria-lysosome contacts transfer protons to acidify lysosomes. - Aging disrupts contacts, causing lysosomal de-acidification and senescence. - Restoring contacts reverses senescence and restores autophagic flux. Source This signal is based on Mitochondria-lysosome coupling contributes to lysosome acidification and aging. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context. Health note: Basic science study; not yet a clinical therapy.
